haiku-low.q1: None. Both return the same 401 page with the same message, "Invalid email or password". For unknown emails, bcrypt runs against a dummy hash, so timing matches.
haiku-low.q2: It gets 429 "too many attempts" with Retry-After 900. No bcrypt check runs, no failure is recorded, and the lock is not extended.
haiku-low.q3: The login transaction deletes the session the incoming cookie points to, then inserts a new session with a new ID. The old ID is dead before the response.
haiku-low.q4: Only the session ID: 32 random bytes, base64url-encoded. It holds no user data. HttpOnly means page scripts cannot read it.
haiku-low.q5: It stops 12 hours after login, when absolute_expires_at passes. Each request only restarts the 30-minute idle timer, so the absolute limit is never extended.
haiku-low.q6: It returns 302 redirect to /login and sets a cookie that clears the session. The session is treated as absent.
haiku-low.q7: The server deletes the session row matching the cookie ID before responding. If none exists, it still gives the same 302 to /login with the cookie cleared.
haiku-low.q8: In the Postgres database, in a sessions table. Both instances read and write the same rows, so any instance finds the session there.
haiku-low.q9: In the login_failures table, one row per failed attempt with email_key and failed_at timestamptz. Counting rows with failed_at in the last 10 minutes decides the window.
haiku-low.q10: It compares last_seen_at to within 30 minutes and absolute_expires_at to the future, both checked by the database. When valid it writes last_seen_at = now().
haiku-low.q11: 503 with the message "We cannot sign you in right now. Try again." The whole transaction is rolled back, so no session is created.
haiku-low.q12: A background job on each instance runs every 10 minutes, deleting dead rows in batches: expired sessions, old failure rows, and ended lock rows.

sonnet.q1: They do not differ. Both return the same 401 login page with 'Invalid email or password', and take about the same time because bcrypt verify runs against a dummy hash.
sonnet.q2: The email is locked: the attempt returns 429 with Retry-After 900, with no bcrypt check, no failure recorded, and the lock is not extended. (Strictly, the 5th failure itself returns 401 and creates the lock; later attempts get 429.)
sonnet.q3: In the same transaction as login, the server deletes the session that the incoming cookie points to (if any) and inserts a new session with a new ID. The old ID is dead before the response is sent.
sonnet.q4: Only the random session ID (32 random bytes, base64url, 43 chars); no user data. The cookie is HttpOnly, so page scripts cannot read it.
sonnet.q5: 12 hours after login (absolute_expires_at, set once and never extended), even though idle refreshes keep the 30-minute idle timer alive.
sonnet.q6: The UPDATE returns no row, so the server responds 302 to /login with a Set-Cookie clearing the session cookie.
sonnet.q7: The server deletes the sessions row matching the cookie ID's hash (0 or 1 row) before responding with 302 to /login and a Set-Cookie clearing the cookie. If the session is already gone, the delete affects 0 rows and the result is the same 302 with the cookie cleared. If there is no cookie, same 302 clearing. A storage error gives 503 'Sign-out failed. Try again.' with the cookie unchanged.
sonnet.q8: In the sessions table in the shared Postgres database. Either instance hashes the cookie's session ID with SHA-256 and looks up id_hash in that table via the UPDATE ... RETURNING user_id statement.
sonnet.q9: In the Postgres login_failures table (one row per failed attempt: email_key, failed_at), plus login_locks for locks. The server counts rows for the email_key whose failed_at is within the last 10 minutes (sliding window, using the database now() clock), and locks at 5 or more.
sonnet.q10: It compares last_seen_at (must be within the last 30 minutes) and absolute_expires_at (must be in the future) against the database now(), and matches the hash of the session ID. If valid, it writes last_seen_at = now() and returns user_id, all in one conditional UPDATE.
sonnet.q11: A 503 response with 'We cannot sign you in right now. Try again.' The whole transaction is rolled back, so no session is created (and no cookie is set as per the document).
sonnet.q12: A background job: every 10 minutes each instance runs a batched delete of dead rows (sessions whose last_seen_at is over 30 minutes old or whose absolute_expires_at has passed). Meanwhile expired rows are never honored.
